newsitem.title: CANADA: Caledonia increases Zambia cobalt tonnage.
newsitem.headline: Caledonia increases Zambia cobalt tonnage.

text.p: Caledonia Mining Corp said on Wednesday it increased the tonnage at its Nama cobalt oxide project in Zambia.
New calculations boosted the indicated and inferred mineral resource at the project to almost 296 million tonnes from 218 million tonnes, the company said.
The cobalt grade for the project was 0.030 percent at a cutoff of 0.015 percent, Caledonia said.
The calculations included tonnage and grade estimates for Caledonia's Nama Anomaly B cobalt. Resources in anomalies A and C were previously announced.
Anomaly B contains an inferred resource of 58 million tonnes at 0.025 percent cobalt equivalent using a 0.015 percent cutoff.
Using a 0.03 percent cutoff, the resource is 13 million tonnes at 0.040 percent.
The anomaly is open to the west, Caledonia said.
Calculations were done by Watts, Griffis and McOuat Ltd of Toronto.
